article.title: は contraste
article.part: Arquitectura básica de la oración — 文の基本構造
article.chapter: Tópico, sujeto y contraste: は/が — 主題・主語・対比：は／が

claims.summary: The particle は can mark contrast between one thing and another, presenting an element as a frame and suggesting that what is said about it may differ from what occurs with another element.
Contrast can be explicit, such as in two parallel phrases, or implicit. 今日は行きます can mean 'I go today' but also imply 'today yes' in a certain context, contrasting with other days.

Examples include '肉は食べます。魚は食べません。' (Meat is eaten; fish is not eaten), '今日は行きます。' (I go today; can imply 'I will go today'), 'コーヒーは飲みますが、お茶は飲みません。' (I drink coffee, but not tea), and 'これは好きです。あれは好きではありません。' (This I like; that I do not like).

links.notes: The Japan Foundation webpage provides a clear definition of the particle は's role in marking contrast, supporting the claim that it can be used to present a contrast between elements.
The Japan Foundation webpage explains how the particle は can express contrast both explicitly and implicitly, providing examples that align with the claim.
